handbookNote: Oklahoma Commercial Driver's License Manual (base AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' content, cover-stamped Version: March 2025; individual section footers mostly read 'Version: July 2017' as in other AAMVA-base states, EXCEPT Section 11 Vehicle Inspection, whose own footer reads 'Version: March 2025' -- a genuine content-level update, not just a cover-page stamp, see below), published by Service Oklahoma -- fetched directly from https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/service-oklahoma/Documents/CDLDriverManual.pdf on 2026-08-23 (5.1MB PDF, 165 pages, linked from the official 'Commercial Driving CDL' and 'CDL First-Time Applicants' pages on oklahoma.gov/service, full text extracted via pdftotext -layout to scratchpad/ok_cdl_research/ok_cdl_manual_full.txt, 9,577 lines). Price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Agency confirmed: per the task brief's warning that Oklahoma driver licensing transitioned from the Department of Public Safety (DPS) to Service Oklahoma mid-pipeline (documented in this project's ok_driver.json), the SAME transition applies to CDL testing specifically -- confirmed via Service Oklahoma's own 'CDL First-Time Applicants' page ('Service Oklahoma administers CDL knowledge and skills testing through its Licensing Offices and authorized third-party examiners') and a March 27, 2025 Service Oklahoma press release ('New CDL Testing Enhancements Improve Efficiency and Readiness for Oklahoma's Commercial Drivers': 'Service Oklahoma administers CDL testing statewide, working with state-owned facilities, commercial truck driving schools, and third-party examiners'), and independently corroborated by the Oklahoma Administrative Code itself: the current Written Examination rule (260:135-5-166) carries the history note 'Transferred from 595:11-3-6 by HB 3419 (2022), eff. 5/19/2022; Amended by Oklahoma Register, Volume 40, Issue 24, September 1, 2023, eff. 9/11/2023' -- i.e. CDL knowledge-test rulemaking itself moved from the old DPS title (595, Chapter 11) to Service Oklahoma's own title (260, Chapter 135, Subchapter 5) in 2022. Exam mechanics are CONFIRMED (not hedged) directly from this official Oklahoma Administrative Code citation (260:135-5-166, 'Written Examination'), fetched via the Cornell Law School Legal Information Institute's regulations mirror (law.cornell.edu/regulations/oklahoma/OAC-260-135-5-166) and cross-checked against Justia's citation listing (regulations.justia.com/states/oklahoma/title-260/chapter-135/subchapter-5/part-29/section-260-135-5-166/) -- both are secondary republications of the official Oklahoma Administrative Code, which is itself maintained by the Oklahoma Secretary of State's Office of Administrative Rules (sos.ok.gov/oar); the underlying CDL manual PDF and Service Oklahoma's own consumer-facing web pages do NOT state these item counts, so this rule citation is the authoritative source. Confirmed figures, all at an 80% minimum passing score except the unrelated motorcycle (M) endorsement (75%, not used by this CDL track): General Knowledge -- minimum 50 multiple-choice questions; Class A Combination Vehicle test -- minimum 20 questions; Air Brakes test -- 25 questions (failing this specific portion results in restriction code 'L', no full air brakes, being placed on the license); Passenger (P), Tank (N), School Bus (S), and Doubles/Triples (T) endorsement tests -- 20 questions each; Hazardous Materials (H) endorsement test -- 30 questions. This is a more precisely sourced mechanics table than most other CDL-track states built in this project, since it comes from a primary state regulatory citation rather than manual front matter or a third-party aggregator. Additional confirmed Oklahoma-specific administrative facts, sourced from Service Oklahoma's own web pages (oklahoma.gov/service/all-pages/cdl-first-time-applicants.html, oklahoma.gov/service/popular-services/cdl.html, oklahoma.gov/service/all-pages/endorsements-and-restrictions.html) since the manual PDF itself carries zero Oklahoma-specific front matter (see below): a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) must be held at least 14 full days (not counting the day of issuance) before the CDL drive/skills test; Entry-Level Driver Training (ELDT) from an FMCSA Training Provider Registry-listed provider is required before the skills test (recommended before the written test), with an exception for prior CDL holders; a DOT Medical Card is required only for drivers who self-certify as 'Non-Excepted Interstate' (not required for Excepted Interstate, Non-Excepted Intrastate, or Excepted Intrastate); Service Oklahoma stopped accepting paper Medical Examiner Certificates as of February 17, 2026; 4-year CDL credential fees are Class A $81.50 ($25 application + $56.50 credential), Class B $71.50, Class C $61.50; the CDL drive/skills test has three components taken in order (pre-trip inspection, basic control skills test, road test), each scored so that a passed section is retained as credit if a later section is failed; the written test may be administered by Service Oklahoma directly or by contracted 'Written Examination Proctors.' Notable structural finding: unlike most other AAMVA-base CDL manuals already built in this project (e.g. New Mexico, Montana, Kentucky, Louisiana), Oklahoma's copy of Sections 1 through 10 carries ZERO Oklahoma-specific front-matter or inline customization anywhere -- confirmed by an exhaustive keyword search of the full extracted text for the word 'Oklahoma' itself, which produced no matches in that range. Section 11 (Vehicle Inspection) is the one genuine exception: its own page-footer version stamp reads 'Version: March 2025' (versus 'Version: July 2017' for every other section), and its content has been fully replaced with Oklahoma's own modernized, item-by-item CDL Vehicle Inspection Test checklist format -- a detailed 4-part air brake check with specific psi thresholds (governor cutout ~120-140 psi, leakage rate max 3 psi/minute single vehicle or 4 psi/minute combination, low-air warning before 55 psi, parking/emergency brake valve pop-out between 20-45 psi), a parallel hydraulic brake check procedure, and separate Class A / Class B-or-C straight-vehicle / Class B-or-C passenger-or-school-bus checklists each marking certain items (brake checks) as automatic-failure if not performed correctly. This exactly matches the scope of the March 27, 2025 Service Oklahoma press release ('New CDL Testing Enhancements'), which announced a modernized CDL skills test effective March 25, 2025 statewide (April 2025 for commercial truck driving schools) -- reducing the pre-trip inspection portion from 40 to about 15 minutes and standardizing the Basic Control Skills Test to four exercises (Forward Stop, Straight-Line Backing, Forward Offset Tracking, Reverse Offset Backing); Section 12 of the fetched manual text independently confirms this same four-exercise structure with detailed scoring rules (pull-ups, encroachments, 'looks'), corroborating that the fetched PDF is the current post-reform edition rather than a stale copy. Bucket structure: the standard 14-bucket convention used across this project's other CDL-track states -- 01_licensing (Section 1 Introduction plus the Oklahoma-specific administrative facts and OAC exam-mechanics table above), 02_driving_safely_a (Section 2, subsections 2.1-2.16), 03_driving_safely_b (Section 2, subsections 2.17-2.23), 04_cargo (Section 3), 05_passenger (Section 4), 06_air_brakes (Section 5), 07_combination (Section 6), 08_doubles_triples (Section 7), 09_tank (Section 8), 10_hazmat_a (Section 9, subsections 9.1-9.4), 11_hazmat_b (Section 9, subsections 9.5-9.8), 12_school_bus (Section 10), 13_vehicle_inspection (Section 11, the March-2025-updated checklist content described above), and 14_basic_control_onroad (Sections 12 and 13 combined). Two content-boundary issues were found and corrected during top-level verification of this build, since sub-agents draft in parallel from assigned line ranges that occasionally mis-locate exact section boundaries in the pdftotext-extracted two-column layout: (1) Section 7 (Doubles and Triples) actually begins at line 5477 of the extracted text, not the originally estimated 5538 -- the drafting agent caught this itself and read the extra lines rather than omitting the 7.1 'Pulling Double/Triple Trailers' hazard-discussion subsection. (2) Section 8 (Tank Vehicles) had an approximately 63-line gap (the section's own introduction, including the tank-endorsement capacity thresholds of 119 gallons individual/1,000 gallons aggregate, Subsection 8.1 Inspecting Tank Vehicles in full, and the start of Subsection 8.2.1 High Center of Gravity) that fell between the line ranges assigned to the doubles/triples and tank-vehicle drafting agents and was consequently never drafted by either -- caught by the lead agent while investigating an unrelated content-boundary question, and personally filled with 10 additional grounded questions appended to 09_tank.json before this build. Every question in this bank is grounded in either a specific passage of the fetched official Oklahoma manual text, an official Service Oklahoma web page, or the cited Oklahoma Administrative Code section -- none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers; all numeric specifications (air brake psi thresholds, tire tread depth minimums, exam item counts and passing scores, capacity thresholds, fee amounts) were verified against the actual sources read during drafting and re-verified independently by the lead agent, not assumed from other states' manuals even where base AAMVA content is textually identical. Answer-choice balance was checked across the full, final 701-question bank: A 26.8%, B 26.4%, C 23.5%, D 23.3%, comfortably inside this project's 15-35% per-letter target, with every individual bucket file also independently inside that band (one bucket's letter distribution was found skewed during a race with a background drafting agent and was mechanically rebalanced, preserving all question/answer text, before this build).
